user_state: Afraid. Avoidant. Knows what they need to do but is paralyzed. Confusing fear with inability.

arrival.heading: You are afraid. That is honest.
arrival.subheading: Fear and forward movement are not opposites. They can exist at the same time.

arrival.heading: Ready is not a feeling.
arrival.subheading: It is a choice. You can choose it before the feeling arrives.

arrival.heading: The fear is real.
arrival.subheading: So is your ability to move alongside it. Both are true.

arrival.heading: You have waited to feel ready.
arrival.subheading: It hasn't come. And that wait has its own weight. The next small step doesn't require readiness.

arrival.heading: Imperfect and done.
arrival.subheading: That is always more useful than perfect and waiting.

arrival.heading: The avoidance is costing you.
arrival.subheading: Not because you are weak. Because the fear has been making decisions.

arrival.heading: One step.
arrival.subheading: Not the whole thing. Not with certainty. Just one step, with the fear alongside.

release.heading: What are you afraid of?
release.subheading: Name it directly. The vague fear is harder to move through than the named one.
release.field_placeholder: What specifically are you afraid will happen...

release.heading: What are you avoiding?
release.subheading: Not why. Just what. Name the thing itself.
release.field_placeholder: The thing you have been circling instead of doing...

release.heading: What is the fear asking you to protect?
release.subheading: It is guarding something. What does it think is at stake?
release.field_placeholder: What is the fear trying to protect you from...

release.heading: What would you do if you were not afraid?
release.subheading: Write it. That is the direction.
release.field_placeholder: Without the fear, what would your next step be...

release.heading: What has the avoidance already cost you?
release.field_placeholder: What has waiting cost you so far...

release.heading: The worst version you are imagining.
release.subheading: Write it down. Then notice how often that exact thing has happened before.
release.field_placeholder: Describe the worst-case scenario your mind is running...

release.heading: What do you already know you need to do?
release.field_placeholder: The thing you already know, that you are still not doing...

breath.heading: Breathe like someone who has decided.
breath.instruction: Slow inhale. Hold briefly. Long exhale. The body follows the breath into steadiness.

breath.heading: The breath before the step.
breath.instruction: One full inhale. One full exhale. Then move. Just that.

breath.heading: Steady.
breath.instruction: Four counts in. Four hold. Four out. Repeat. Courage lives in steady breathing.

breath.heading: Breathe through the resistance.
breath.instruction: The body tightens before action. Breathe into the tightness. Three times.

breath.heading: Ground before you go.
breath.instruction: Feel your feet on the floor. Breathe once, fully. Then take the first step.

What is the smallest version of the step you are afraid of?
What would imperfect action look like today?
What is the fear protecting? What does it think it's guarding?

completion.heading: You moved alongside the fear.
completion.subheading: That is not the absence of courage. That is exactly what it is.

completion.heading: Imperfect and done.
completion.subheading: You did the thing. The fear was there. You went anyway.

completion.heading: You chose forward.
completion.subheading: Not because it was easy. Because you decided it mattered more.

completion.heading: The step happened.
completion.subheading: Small or large. Perfect or rough. It happened. That counts.

completion.heading: You were afraid.
completion.subheading: And you did it anyway. That is something to carry forward.

completion.heading: Ready never arrived.
completion.subheading: You went without it. That is the definition of the thing.

completion.heading: You showed up to the thing.
completion.subheading: Not to the version where everything went perfectly. To the real thing.

home_cards.headline: Ready is a decision, not a feeling.
home_cards.subheadline: You can decide before the feeling arrives.

home_cards.headline: The fear is real and so is the next step.
home_cards.subheadline: Both are true at the same time.

home_cards.headline: Waiting to feel ready has its own weight.
home_cards.subheadline: Small movement, even imperfect, is lighter than staying still.

home_cards.headline: Imperfect action is always better than perfect waiting.
home_cards.subheadline: The gap between them is where avoidance lives.

home_cards.headline: You are not avoiding because you are weak.
home_cards.subheadline: You are avoiding because the fear is making decisions.

home_cards.headline: The smallest step is still a step.
Something in you already knows the direction.
home_cards.subheadline: The next step doesn't need to be the whole answer.

home_cards.headline: Courage is not the absence of fear.
home_cards.subheadline: It is moving alongside it. That is what you are doing.

home_cards.headline: The thing you're avoiding knows you're nearby.
home_cards.subheadline: You've been circling it. Today you can step closer.

home_cards.headline: The outcome is not the only thing.
home_cards.subheadline: The act of choosing is also something.

home_cards.headline: Fear and forward movement can coexist.
home_cards.subheadline: You don't have to wait for the fear to leave.

home_cards.headline: Done imperfectly is still done.
home_cards.subheadline: Perfectionism keeps the door closed. Imperfect action opens it.

home_cards.headline: One step is not the whole thing.
home_cards.subheadline: It is just the step. That is all that is being asked.

home_cards.headline: The fear has been running the schedule.
home_cards.subheadline: Today you can take back one item on that schedule.

actions.content: Write down the one thing you have been avoiding. Just name it. No plan yet.
actions.why: Naming it brings it out of the imagination, where it is larger, into reality.

actions.content: Do the first 5% of the avoided task. Nothing more.
actions.why: Starting is the barrier. The first step is always harder than the second.

actions.content: Send the message, make the call, or write the email you have been delaying.
actions.why: Delayed communication costs more in anxiety than the discomfort of sending.

actions.content: Write: 'What I am afraid of is ___. What I will do anyway is ___.'
actions.why: Holding both truths simultaneously is how you move through rather than around.

actions.content: Tell one person about the thing you've been avoiding. Just the fact of avoiding it.
actions.why: Saying it aloud reduces the shame that reinforces avoidance.

actions.content: Schedule the avoided thing in your calendar for today. Block the time.
actions.why: Intention without scheduling rarely becomes action. Make it an appointment.

actions.content: Do the hard thing first. Before checking messages, email, or notifications.
actions.why: The avoided task grows when you face everything else first.

actions.content: Write down the worst realistic outcome of taking the step. Then write: 'And I could live with that.'
actions.why: The imagined worst-case is almost always something you could live through. Making it concrete reduces its power.

actions.content: Set a two-minute timer. Work on the feared task only until it ends.
actions.why: Two minutes is almost always enough to prove you can start.

actions.content: Ask for help with the thing you have been trying to handle alone.
actions.why: Asking for help is a form of courage. Isolation reinforces avoidance.

actions.content: Write down three times you did a hard thing without feeling ready first.
actions.why: Evidence of past courage is the most credible argument against the current fear.

actions.content: Make the decision you have been delaying. Not the perfect one. The next one.
actions.why: A made decision, even an imperfect one, costs less than an unmade one.

actions.content: Write one sentence about what you want. Not what you think is realistic. What you want.
actions.why: Fear often silences wanting. Naming it restores the direction.

actions.content: Do one thing today that requires other people to see you.
actions.why: Being seen is often what avoidance is quietly protecting against. One small moment of visibility changes what feels possible.

actions.content: Write down the first reason your fear gives for not taking the step. Then ask: is that actually true?
actions.why: Naming the fear's argument and gently questioning it changes how much space it takes up.

actions.content: Go to the place or open the thing you have been avoiding. Just arrive. Nothing more yet.
actions.why: Physical arrival changes the internal state. Presence is its own kind of progress.

actions.content: Write a letter to yourself from one year from now, assuming you took the step.
actions.why: Future perspective reduces the weight the present moment is carrying.

actions.content: Apologize for something you have been avoiding apologizing for.
actions.why: The dread of apologizing is almost always longer-lasting than the apology itself.

actions.content: Raise your hand, your voice, or your idea in the next available moment.
actions.why: Small moments of being seen tend to make the next one a little easier.

actions.content: Write down what you actually think. About the hard thing. Your real opinion.
actions.why: Suppressing a real view costs energy and grows avoidance.

actions.content: Say no to the thing you agreed to out of fear of disappointing someone.
actions.why: Fear-based yes is not generosity. Honest no is its own form of courage.

actions.content: Start the project before it is perfect. Write the draft, submit the rough version.
actions.why: Waiting for perfect is usually waiting for a feeling that won't come before you begin.

actions.content: Write about the fear as if it were a separate voice. What does it say? Then write what you know to be true alongside that.
actions.why: Giving the fear a voice outside of you creates some distance. From that distance, it is easier to see what it actually is.

actions.content: Take the step you've been afraid of in a smaller context first.
actions.why: A smaller version of the same step shows you the feeling of doing it. That changes what the larger version seems like.

actions.content: Tell the truth about something you have been softening.
actions.why: Softening what is true gradually costs something. A moment of honesty, even small, restores something.

actions.content: Publish, send, or share the thing you have been holding back.
actions.why: The barrier between done and sent is often only fear of being seen.

actions.content: Set a boundary you have been afraid to set.
actions.why: Boundaries protect what matters. Fear of setting them gives away what matters.

actions.content: Write what you would tell a friend who was facing exactly what you are facing.
actions.why: The counsel you give freely to others is usually what you need most.

actions.content: Do the thing in a way you know is imperfect. Let imperfect be enough.
actions.why: Imperfection is not the barrier. The belief that imperfection is not allowed is. This removes that belief.

actions.content: Commit out loud: 'I will do ___ today, even though I am afraid.'
actions.why: Saying it aloud changes something. The voice makes it real in a way that staying in the mind does not.

What part of you already knows what to do?
What would happen if the fear turned out to be wrong?

What has waiting been like? What does it feel like in your body to stay here?
What does imperfect action look like for the thing you are avoiding?
What is the fear protecting you from that you might not actually need protecting from?
What would you start if you knew it was okay to start badly?
What has the avoidance been like for your body? Your sleep? Your focus?
What feels different about you when you take a step despite the fear?
What is the thing you want so much that the fear of failing it is this strong?
What have you been rehearsing in your head instead of doing?
What would forward movement look like today? Not eventually. Today.
What would you do if no one was watching and judgment was not possible?

What is the most courageous small thing you could do today?

What would it mean to you if this situation stayed exactly as it is?
What is the fear trying to preserve? Is it working?
Imagine taking the step. What does that feel like from the inside? What happens first?
